Q: Missing first month in bar chart using R and Rstudio A:

Don't use scale_x_date with labels and breaks, there are date_labels and date_breaks to set date labels' formats and breaks. In the code below I will not use them. Since there are only two months, I will coerce to factor instead.

First, define a custom theme, with the colors, rotated x axis labels, etc.

theme_custom_q79974513 <- function(){ 
  theme_bw() %+replace%
    theme(
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, angle = 90, vjust = 0.5),
      # axis.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15, angle  = 45, vjust = 0.5),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#add8e6"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eceff8"),
      panel.border = element_rect(colour = "#bdbdd3", linewidth = 2.5),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#eceff8")
    )
}

Now the plot.
The years and months are created and the data is aggregated in a dplyr pipe, then plotted.

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

myColors <- c("OSHA" = "#CB1006", "Non OSHA" = "#1BE4B9")

my_group %>%
  mutate(
    Month = as.Date(Month),
    Year = format(Month, "%Y"),
    Month = format(Month, "%b") |> factor(levels = month.abb)
  ) %>%
  summarise(Incidents = sum(Incidents), .by = c(Category, Year, Month)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Month, Incidents, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Incidents, color = Category), 
    position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE, vjust = 0.5), 
    size = 5, 
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = myColors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("OSHA" = "white", "Non OSHA" = "black")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,15), breaks = seq(0,15,1)) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ Year) +
  theme_custom_q79974513()

Created on 2026-07-05 with reprex v2.1.1

Test data

set.seed(1)
n <- 20L
Incidents <- rep(1, n)
Category <- sample(c("OSHA", "Non OSHA"), n, TRUE) |> factor(levels = c("OSHA", "Non OSHA"))
Month <- sprintf("20%02d-%02d-%02d", 
                 c(rep(26:25, times = c(7, 4)), rep(26:25, times = c(5, 4))),
                 rep(1:2, times = c(11, 9)),
                 c(rep(26:25, times = c(7, 4)), rep(26:25, times = c(5, 4))))
my_group <- data.frame(Incidents, Category, Month)

Q: How do apps like Instagram/X keep post state (e.g. likes) synchronized across different feeds in SwiftUI? A:

Some apps probably do fetch per screen, some will fetch into a central store, others will fetch to a central store which is cached to disk.

To migrate from view-based to store-based loading, remove @State and .task and instead make an @Observable class PostStore and make it load in its init. To make the store be central, if you are targeting iOS 27 you can use @State, but if lower you need to either conform the class to ObservableObject and use @StateObject, use fileprivate global var or singleton.

You need to fetch the posts in init and when receiving push notification from server, in timer or in app lifecycle notification. Then you need to monitor all the post objects for changes and in a delayed/coalesced func (or lifecycle notification and background task) send the changes to the server.

By the way when your model is an object in a central store, like your Post class, you should use .self as the id in List, i.e. identify it by its pointer. You can also conform to Identifiable and use var id: ObjectIdentifier { ObjectIdentifier(self) }.

Q: How to check a text file to see if it contains the value of a string variable A:

If you change your check to lines.contains(test) it will work perfectly.

Why?

The problem is that lines.contains("$test") will eventually call String.equals(Object obj) and although could seem a little bit strange at first but test.equals("$test") returns false as "$test" is a GString and not a String.
